correctness.rationale: Fourier inversion computes kernel k(0)=(p−1)(u+v)/(2p) and k(x)=−(u+v)/(2p)+epsilon_p sqrt(p)chi_p(x)(u−v)/(2p) for nonzero x. The classical quadratic Gauss sign makes the nonzero kernel magnitudes equal for p≡1 mod4, and of two real absolute values for p≡3 mod4. The complex induced endpoint norm equals the full row absolute sum. Cauchy–Schwarz with kernel squared norm (p−1)/p, followed by its equality condition, proves exact maximizing phases in congruence-one primes. A two-branch linear/Cauchy optimization handles congruence-three primes including the tie at p=3. All maximizing kernel entries are nonzero, so triangle equality classifies inputs. At C5 the Laplacian spectrum agrees with the QR/NQR bands, proving the stated reduced imaginary-power formula. Standalone direct Fourier checks passed for 45 primes and 5 cycle parameters, but the infinite theorem is analytical.

originality.rationale: An exact zero-DC two-band quadratic-residue complex endpoint norm profile, its phase-optimized prime-parity dichotomy and all attaining phase parameters were not covered by the inspected works. Bui et al prove infinite-lattice growth, Benedetto et al characterize unit-DC Björck CAZACs and ambiguity, Green & Green study fixed polyphase sequences and correlations, Sahasranand treats a real two-parameter constant-offdiagonal matrix class. Three relevant mathematical records were read in full and concern Paley fourth moments, Paley Fourier energy concentration or cubic-residue projections. Classical Gauss identities and the congruence-three Björck phase are credited; high residual risk of a historically equivalent Fourier-algebra calculation remains.
residual_risks: Classical cyclotomy, Paley complex sequences, Björck/CAZAC theory and Fourier-algebra Lebesgue constants have extensive historical coverage; an equivalent zero-DC continuous-phase endpoint norm may exist under unfamiliar terminology.
The specific congruence-three optimal phase parameter agrees with the known Björck phase; no priority is claimed for that parameter by itself.
The general quadratic Gauss sum is classical and powerful; the contribution is the full optimized norm/equality classification rather than a new Gauss-sum evaluation.

value.rationale: Two-band phase-only quadratic-residue multipliers are a canonical complete finite-harmonic-analysis family. An exact optimized endpoint norm and all attaining masks give a natural full-prime classification with an arithmetically meaningful parity dichotomy: flat impulse kernels saturate the universal mean-zero l2-derived bound exactly for p≡1 mod4, while the other class has an explicit strict positive gap. This is not a tiny arbitrary calculation; the theorem covers every odd prime, produces quantitative structural obstructions, determines every phase and input equality case, and yields an exact periodic imaginary-power example on the five-cycle. It does not claim general physical design guarantees.
